description: Precise MVP scope for CreatorOS -- resolves 3 conflicting MVP definitions into a single recommended release plan across 5 incremental releases, with explicit exclusions, prerequisite decisions, tech stack, and success criteria. Revised in Phase 14.6F to align with 18 ratified P0 decisions (2026-06-04).
provenance_detail: SYNTHESIZED_CANON for the recommended MVP and release structure. DEC-146B-COS-001 (MVP scope Option B ratified 2026-06-04) and DEC-146B-COS-002 (Clerk auth ratified 2026-06-04, was DEC-145-004). SOURCE_PRESERVED_TRUTH for the 3 conflicting definitions extracted verbatim from Google Doc Tabs 3, 6, and 7.
cross_references: phase14_6b_creatoros_current_implementation_truth.json (16 pages, 20 tables, broken auth, god files)
phase14_6b_creatoros_product_types_commerce_canon.json (10 product types, commerce model, pricing tiers)

mvp_conflict.source: Google Doc Tab 6 (Minimum Viable Product) -- original definition
mvp_conflict.scope: Content distribution + community only. Smallest scope.
mvp_conflict.assessment: Too narrow. The core 'post once publish everywhere' promise requires platform OAuth integrations that are the hardest engineering work. Excludes features the current codebase already has (stories, AI, marketplace page, DMs). Would require REMOVING existing features or hiding them. Also excludes revenue-generating capabilities entirely -- no path to $1 without a follow-up release.

mvp_conflict.source: Google Doc Tab 7 (Copy of Minimum Viable Product) -- expanded definition
mvp_conflict.scope: Content + community + courses + marketplace + payments. Largest MVP scope.
features: Marketplace with product listings and product detail pages
mvp_conflict.assessment: Too broad. Adds courses, marketplace, payments, and subscriptions to the MVP -- each a multi-week build. Combined with the platform integration engineering from Tab 6, this is a 6+ month effort for a solo developer team. The cross-platform OAuth integrations alone (Instagram API, TikTok API, YouTube API, X API) each require app review processes that take weeks. No realistic timeline attached.

mvp_conflict.source: Google Doc Tab 3 (Copy of PRD) -- Build Guide section
mvp_conflict.scope: 7.4-week sprint plan. Partial overlap with both Tab 6 and Tab 7.
explicit_exclusions: Not explicitly stated -- scope implied by sprint breakdown
mvp_conflict.assessment: Most realistic of the three but still aggressive. The 7.4-week timeline assumes greenfield development with Clerk auth from day 1 -- does not account for the existing codebase's broken auth, god files requiring extraction, and Replit-origin code requiring audit. However, the scope (content + community + basic courses + basic marketplace + AI) is close to the recommended Option B from CONTRA-COS-002.

recommended_mvp.scope: Option B: Creator + Course/Product -- content creation, community, basic courses, basic product marketplace, and existing features (AI chat, stories, DMs) stabilized. Cross-platform distribution deferred to post-MVP.
rationale: The current codebase already has partial implementations of content feed, communities, marketplace, AI agents, stories, DMs, and notifications. Building on existing code is faster than greenfield.

Cross-platform distribution (the 'post once publish everywhere' promise) requires platform OAuth integrations (Instagram Graph API, TikTok API, YouTube Data API, X API) that each require app review processes taking 2-6 weeks. This is the hardest engineering with the most external dependency. Deferring it de-risks the MVP.
Courses and products are the revenue-generating features. An MVP without revenue capability has no path to validating the business model.
Option A (Tab 6: content + community only) is too small -- it excludes revenue, courses, and features the code already has.
Option C/D (Tab 7/full PRD) is too large -- includes UGC campaigns, ads platform, editing studio, automation, and cross-posting which are each multi-month builds.

Option B ships a usable creator platform where a creator can: build a profile, post content, host a community, sell digital products, sell courses, and interact with AI -- all within CreatorOS's own ecosystem. Cross-platform distribution makes it MORE powerful later but is not required for the MVP value proposition.
recommended_mvp.value_proposition: CreatorOS MVP lets creators build their brand home base: create content, host a community, sell products and courses, and interact with AI tools -- all from one platform with X/Twitter-inspired clean design.
what_mvp_proves: Creators will adopt a consolidated platform that replaces Gumroad + Discord + Teachable
The commerce model (4-tier pricing + transaction fees) generates revenue
The X/Twitter-inspired design creates retention in the target persona
The content + community + commerce loop creates a self-reinforcing ecosystem
The tech stack (React + Express + Drizzle + Clerk + Neon + Stripe) supports the full product vision
what_mvp_does_not_prove: Cross-platform distribution demand ('post once publish everywhere')
Platform API integration reliability at scale

prerequisite_decisions.description: Operator decisions that MUST be made before R1 development begins. Each decision blocks concrete implementation work.

decisions.question: Which MVP scope is canonical? Three conflicting definitions exist in the Google Doc.

options.A: Creator/Community Only (Tab 6 -- smallest, excludes revenue features)
options.B: Creator + Course/Product (recommended -- content + community + courses + marketplace + payments)
options.C: Creator + Full Distribution (Tab 7-ish -- adds cross-platform publishing to B)
options.D: Full PRD Scope (everything including UGC, ads, automation, editing studio)

decisions.ratified_answer: B — Content + Community + Courses + Sales (8-12 weeks). Operator approved.
decisions.recommendation_rationale: Builds on existing code. Includes revenue. Defers hardest engineering (platform integrations) to post-MVP. Provable business model in 5 releases over ~15 weeks.
decisions.impact: Previously blocked all feature prioritization, sprint planning, and resource allocation. Now UNBLOCKED.

decisions.question: Auth migration strategy for CreatorOS?
decisions.context: Both apps target Clerk. EOS Beast branch already has partial Clerk implementation. CreatorOS has CRITICAL auth bypass (any password works). EOS is closer to revenue (primary focus).

options.A: Fix Passport.js comparePasswords immediately (bandaid), then migrate to Clerk later
options.B: Skip Passport.js fix, migrate directly to Clerk as first task
options.C: Fix Passport.js AND add security hardening, defer Clerk to post-MVP
options.D: Clerk migration as first task, block ALL other implementation until auth is complete

decisions.ratified_answer: D — Clerk first, block ALL other implementation until auth complete. Operator approved. Clerk is confirmed as production auth provider (DEC-146B-EOS-003 also ratifies Clerk for EOS).
decisions.recommendation_rationale: Auth bypass is CRITICAL severity. Fixing Passport.js is wasted work on a system scheduled for replacement. EOS Beast already has Clerk pattern as reference.
decisions.impact: Previously blocked all deployment and feature build. Now UNBLOCKED — Clerk migration is the ratified first task.

decisions.question: Stick with Express or migrate to NestJS? (CONTRA-COS-008)
decisions.context: PRD Tab 3 Tech Architecture says NestJS. Build Guide says Express. Code uses Express. NestJS migration is significant effort with unclear ROI.

options.A: Stay on Express (code already works, split god files into modular routes is sufficient)
options.B: Migrate to NestJS (more structured, better for team scaling, aligns with PRD tech architecture)
options.C: Evaluate Hono or Fastify as lighter alternatives

decisions.recommendation: A -- Stay on Express. The god file problem is solved by splitting routes.ts and storage.ts into domain modules, not by framework migration. NestJS migration delays MVP by weeks with no user-facing benefit.
decisions.impact: Determines backend architecture for all MVP development.

decisions.question: File storage provider for user uploads (images, videos, documents)?
decisions.context: Current code uploads to local disk (uploads/ directory committed to git). Production needs cloud storage.

options.A: Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible, no egress fees, cheapest at scale)

decisions.recommendation: A -- Cloudflare R2. Zero egress fees is critical for a media-heavy creator platform where consumers download content. S3-compatible API means minimal code changes.
decisions.impact: Affects upload middleware, CDN strategy, and cost model. Blocks R2 (content) development.

decisions.question: Video hosting for course lessons?
decisions.context: Course platform (R5) needs video hosting with streaming, adaptive bitrate, and progress tracking.

options.A: Mux (purpose-built for video, excellent API, $0.025/min storage + $0.007/min streaming)
options.B: Cloudflare Stream ($1/1000 min storage, $0.01/1000 min viewed)
options.C: Direct S3/R2 with HLS encoding (DIY, cheapest, most work)

decisions.recommendation: B -- Cloudflare Stream. Pairs with R2 recommendation. Simpler than Mux, cheaper than Mux, good enough for MVP course content. Upgrade path to Mux exists if needed.
decisions.impact: Blocks R5 (courses) development. Can be deferred since R5 is last release.

decisions.question: Confirm Business tier pricing: $79/mo (operator correction OC-COS-011) or $99/mo (PRD Tab 2)?
decisions.context: CONTRA-COS-014 documents this conflict. Operator correction OC-COS-011 states $79. PRD original source states $99.
decisions.recommendation: Defer to operator. Both values are preserved in commerce canon.
decisions.impact: Affects Stripe product configuration and pricing page. Not blocking until R4.

decisions.question: Real-time messaging strategy: WebSocket or polling?
decisions.context: ws 8.18.0 is installed but unused. Community chat and DMs currently use HTTP endpoints. WebSocket enables true real-time. Polling is simpler but creates latency.

options.A: WebSocket via ws (already in dependencies, true real-time)
options.B: Short polling (simple, works everywhere, 2-5 second latency)
options.C: Server-Sent Events (SSE, one-way real-time, simpler than WebSocket)
options.D: Defer real-time, ship with manual refresh / pull-to-refresh

decisions.recommendation: B for R3 MVP, upgrade to A post-MVP. Polling is simpler to implement and debug. Real-time can be layered on without changing the data model.

success_criteria.target: Order state machine handles all transitions: pending -> completed -> refunded. No stuck orders.
success_criteria.measurement: Automated test: create order, confirm payment webhook, verify entitlement, process refund, verify entitlement revoked.

success_criteria.target: Consumer can purchase a course, watch lessons, and see progress percentage update.
success_criteria.measurement: Manual test: purchase -> enroll -> complete 3 of 5 lessons -> verify 60% progress shown.

success_criteria.target: Revenue dashboard numbers match Stripe dashboard within $0.01 tolerance.
success_criteria.measurement: Compare CreatorOS revenue total vs Stripe dashboard for same time period.

success_criteria.target: Minimum 50% line coverage on backend code. 100% coverage on payment and auth flows.
A new creator can go from sign-up to first product listed in under 10 minutes.
success_criteria.measurement: Manual test: time from Clerk sign-up to published product in marketplace.

success_criteria.target: tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors on every release.
success_criteria.measurement: CI pipeline includes tsc check. No ts-ignore comments in new code.

success_criteria.target: Dark mode default. X/Twitter-inspired minimalism. No glassmorphism. No gamification chrome.
success_criteria.measurement: Visual review against design identity canon. theme.json appearance='dark'.

total_estimated_timeline.caveat: Timeline assumes CreatorOS gets dedicated development attention. If CreatorOS is nights/weekends only (current reality per CLAUDE.md: 'Future side projects are not being actively worked on'), elapsed calendar time will be 3-5x longer than effort weeks. EOS and Initiate Arena are the current priorities.
total_estimated_timeline.dependency_on_eos: Clerk migration pattern established in EOS (DEC-146B-EOS-003 ratified Clerk for EOS) will template CreatorOS R1, reducing auth migration effort. Both auth decisions ratified 2026-06-04.

post_mvp_roadmap_sketch.note: Not part of the MVP specification. Included for context on what follows the 5 releases.

r6.name: Cross-Platform Distribution
r6.scope: Platform OAuth connections (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X). Universal publisher. Content calendar. Scheduling. Per-platform preview. This is the 'post once publish everywhere' promise.
r6.prerequisite: Platform API app approvals (2-6 weeks each)

r7.name: Subscriptions + Memberships
r7.scope: Stripe subscription billing. Creator membership tiers. Bundled access. Grace periods. Billing portal.

r8.name: Automation + Email
r8.scope: Visual automation builder. Email/newsletter system. Trigger-based workflows (new follower -> welcome DM, purchase -> course enrollment).

r9.name: Analytics Dashboard
r9.scope: Cross-platform analytics (post-R6). Unified audience insights. Content performance. Revenue attribution.

r10.name: UGC + Ads Platform
r10.scope: UGC campaign management for brands. Self-serve ads platform for in-feed promotion.
r10.prerequisite: Significant user base. Brand advertiser demand.

umh_integration.name: UMH Substrate Activation
umh_integration.scope: Activate dormant projection code. Add umh_status columns and umh_outcomes table. Enable UMH signal emission from CreatorOS events. Enable UMH capability execution from CreatorOS context.
umh_integration.prerequisite: CreatorOS production deployment + UMH substrate production deployment

risk_register.description: Entire codebase was authored by Replit Agent. Code quality is unaudited. Hidden bugs, inconsistent patterns, and security issues are likely. Every existing feature needs audit before stabilization.
risk_register.mitigation: Thorough code review during R1 god file split. Automated tests for every stabilized feature. TypeScript strict mode.

risk_register.risk: God file split breaks existing features
risk_register.description: Splitting routes.ts (53KB, 89 routes) and storage.ts (104KB) into domain modules risks introducing bugs in the extraction. No existing tests to catch regressions.
risk_register.mitigation: Write integration tests for all existing routes BEFORE splitting. Use git bisect if regression found. Split one domain at a time, test after each.

risk_register.description: Stripe Connect Express accounts have onboarding requirements, compliance checks, and payout schedules that add complexity beyond simple Stripe Checkout.
risk_register.mitigation: Start Stripe setup in R1 (create platform account). Prototype checkout flow in staging before R4 development begins. Use Stripe test mode extensively.

risk_register.description: The core product promise is 'post once publish everywhere.' The MVP defers this to R6. This means the MVP does not deliver the primary differentiator.
risk_register.mitigation: Position MVP as 'creator home base' not 'distribution hub.' Cross-platform is a known post-MVP priority. The MVP value is consolidation (community + products + courses in one place), not distribution.

risk_register.risk: CreatorOS deprioritized behind EOS and Initiate Arena
risk_register.description: Per CLAUDE.md, current priorities are Initiate Arena -> personal brand -> OS repo. CreatorOS is 'nights/weekends only until primary focus is generating.' Calendar timeline will be 3-5x effort timeline.
risk_register.mitigation: Accept the extended calendar timeline. Use MVP specification to enable efficient work during available windows. Clerk pattern from EOS will accelerate R1.
